narrative: The model estimated a 25% chance that you would be a bad credit risk. Although that means most applicants with your profile would not default, it is above the bank’s approval cutoff, so your application was denied. In reaching this decision, the model placed greatest weight on the length of the credit request; your six-month term is much shorter than the approved average of about nineteen months, and this counted in your favour. The next most influential factor was checking-account status: having no checking account is the most common situation among approved applicants, and it also lowered your assessed risk. The third was the amount requested; at 3,518 DM it is somewhat above the approved average of about 3,020 DM, but in your case it still worked slightly in your favour. These three leading factors therefore reduced your risk rather than increased it, but other aspects of your profile outweighed them enough to leave the overall risk above the bank’s threshold. To improve your position, ask the lender which remaining factors drove the decision, request a copy of your credit report to check for errors, and consider reapplying after reducing the requested amount, building savings, or providing stronger documentation of your repayment capacity.
